promo-pod-crown.title: Canva's licence bans Pro elements on t-shirts #shorts
promo-pod-crown.description:
Canva's Content Licence Agreement has a list of things you may not do with Pro content, and it names them: use or display the content on venues involving the sale of on demand products, including postcards, mugs, t-shirts, posters.

T-shirts. Named. In the prohibited list.

The same agreement is just as clear the other way about free content — it allows prints and other reproductions for resale. So one element with a crown on it turns a legal product into a licence violation.

And the crown is the only difference you can see. It sits in the corner of the thumbnail in the elements panel, and once the element is on your canvas you cannot see it at all. Filter every element search to Free, every single time.

promo-pod-white-box.title: Why your t-shirt design prints as a white box #shorts
promo-pod-white-box.description:
Your artwork has to sit on nothing. If the PNG exports with a white rectangle behind it, that rectangle prints — a white box on a black shirt — and the first you hear about it is a refund.

Download, PNG, then the setting that matters: transparent background. Canva's help pages are explicit that this one is paid — it is only available on Pro, Teams, Business, Education and Nonprofits.

Then check it. Open the PNG on a dark background. Your computer's preview shows transparency as a chequerboard. If you see white where you expected nothing, the toggle did not take.

promo-pod-irony.title: You need Canva Pro to export it. Pro is what breaks it. #shorts
promo-pod-irony.description:
This is the genuinely silly bit, and nobody says both halves out loud.

You need Canva Pro to export a transparent PNG, because that export is a paid feature. And you must not use Pro elements in the design you are exporting, because Canva's licence names t-shirts in the list of prohibited uses of Pro content.

Both are true at the same time. A free plan can design a legal shirt and cannot export it properly. A Pro plan can export it properly and can very easily make it illegal.

So: pay for Pro for the export, and filter every element search to Free anyway. Knowing that is most of the job.

promo-pod-niche.title: The t-shirts that sell are not the pretty ones #shorts
promo-pod-niche.description:
The shirts that sell are almost never beautiful. They are specific — a phrase that one group of people recognises and everyone else does not.

Which means the research is not what looks good. It is which group am I making this for, and what do they say to each other.

Niche down further than feels sensible. Not nurses — night shift nurses. Not dog owners — people whose greyhound has taken the sofa.

Print on demand is not really a design business. It is a research business with a design step on the end, and the people doing well at it are not better illustrators than you.
